scope: Three implementations of the same GDI rectangle capture inside one Electron main process, on one synthetic opaque top-level window that is painted, made topmost and captured by its own content bounds (1920x1080 display, 100% scale). A is the 872e5b5 TypeScript (Koffi bindings re-created per call, NativeImage result); B keeps the same bindings cached and returns the raw BGRA buffer; C calls the Rust DLL. Interleaved A/B/C/C/B/A order, three warmups then thirty samples per variant per metric. Metrics: buffer (A adds toBitmap), image (nativeImage.createFromBitmap for B/C), thumbnail (capture + resize to 640 wide + toBitmap, i.e. the open() path without PNG or renderer wait), scroll (capture + ScrollCapture.add + preview, so scroll matching time is included but unchanged between variants). Excluded: PNG encoding, renderer/desktopCapturer round trips, UI composition waits, multi-display stitching, 4K real capture (no 4K display here), mixed DPI, UAC/RDP/locked-session behaviour, first DLL load (measured outside the samples), and Windows 11 corner rounding is disabled with DwmSetWindowAttribute so the whole client area is captured. Thirty samples per variant; p95 is nearest-rank. CPU cost is a separate 100-call batch per variant because process.cpuUsage() has 15.6 ms granularity. After the samples, the shipping module src/main/capture-screen.ts is loaded from the working tree and its captureScreenPixels/captureScreen output is compared byte-for-byte with the measured implementations.
